messages:
sara (new hire): Hey team — just started today! My USB4 dock arrived but my external monitor is showing ‘no signal’ and my laptop isn’t getting ethernet. Anyone know who to ask for a quick check?
Alex K: welcome @sara 🎉 pinging @Tanya (IT) — she handled my dock last month. Quick Q: are you on an M-series mac or intel?
Sara (new hire): MacBook Pro M2, macOS 13.6. Dock model is Anker USB4 2-port. Monitor powers on and shows input HDMI-1 but no picture. Ethernet link light on the dock is off.
Tanya (IT): hi @sara — welcome! I can help. Quick troubleshooting before I swing by: 1) Try a different USB-C cable (some cables are power-only), 2) On mac: Apple menu > About This Mac > System Report > Thunderbolt to confirm device shows up, 3) Run this in Terminal and paste output: networksetup -listallhardwareports && ifconfig en0 | grep inet
Sara (new hire): trying cable swap now.
Sara (new hire): Terminal output: 
---
Hardware Port: Wi-Fi
Device: en0
Ethernet Address: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff

no en1 entry for thunderbolt, ifconfig en0 shows ipadress 192.168.86.21 (wifi)
---
Also tried a different HDMI cable -> still blank.
Tanya (IT): thanks — sounds like the dock isn't enumerating over TB. Can you reboot with the dock connected? Also press the power button on the dock (some Anker units have a tiny switch). If still no device, try SMC/NVRAM reset steps for Apple silicon: shut down, wait 30s, power on while holding power until startup-options appear -> then restart.
Sara (new hire): rebooted with dock connected, still no luck. power button on dock didn't do anything.
Tanya (IT): OK creating an IT ticket and will bring a spare TB4 adapter and a tested dock. Ticket TICKET-4829 created for pickup at HQ desk. device-bot: IT ticket created: TICKET-4829 by Tanya (IT). ETA: today 3pm. Tracking: https://it.redwood.example/tickets/TICKET-4829
Bob Ops: there’s also a drawer in the common IT closet (2nd floor) with spare USB-C -> HDMI adapters. If you want a quick stop, I can drop one at reception.
Sara (new hire): thanks @Bob Ops — I’m near reception now, grabbed a spare active USB-C->HDMI dongle and plugged it into the dock port, monitor lit up! Ethernet still dead though.
Tanya (IT): good progress — that tells us the dock’s HDMI passthrough works but TB controller might be flaky for MAC host. For ethernet: when you plug the dock in, does System Settings > Network show a new interface (USB 10/100/1000)? If not, I’ll swap docks. Also ifconfig | grep -A3 en5 (or en4) might show it.
Sara (new hire): network panel shows only Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth PAN, no wired. ifconfig doesn't show en4/en5.
Tanya (IT): thanks — I’ll bring a replacement dock+tested cable and the spare TB4 adapter. I marked the ticket high priority since onboarding setup blocked. ETA 2:30pm.
Sara (new hire): awesome, thx! one more quick newbies Q — who do I add for badge/access?
Alex K: ping People Ops channel or DM @Maya in people-ops. She sorted my badge in 10m.
Tanya (IT): dropped by at 2:20pm, swapped the dock and cable, verified ethernet link and monitor. Confirmed everything works on the replacement unit. Left the original dock in Ops for diagnostics.
device-bot: TICKET-4829 updated: resolved by Tanya (IT) — status: resolved.
Sara (new hire): everything works now, thanks so much! saving this thread for future reference :thumbsup:
Alex K: welcome aboard again! happy to help with onboarding checklist—DM me when you have 10.
Tanya (IT): leaving notes on ticket: vendor RMA recommended if original dock fails diagnostics. If anyone else sees similar behavior, swap cable first (active TB4 cable) then swap dock.
Sara (new hire): noted, thanks team 🙂
